blocks.title: Comparative Adjectives and Adverbs of One and Two Syllables: ___er … Than

items.q: Mary’s handwriting is clear. Joe’s handwriting is very clear.
A motorcycle runs fast. A car runs very fast.
Daniel is nice. Charlie is very nice.
Mr. Romero is busy. Mr. Peyton is very busy.
The grammar teacher dictates quick. The English teacher dictates very quick.
A Math test is easy. An English test is very easy.
A young person is happy. A child is very happy.
Johana is pretty. Katherine is very pretty.
A car is heavy. An airplane is very heavy.
I get up early. My mother gets up very early.
Claudia is thin. Miriam is very thin.
The dictionary is thick. The Math book is very thick.
An athlete is strong. A wrestler is very strong.
A person who doesn’t eat enough is weak. A sick person is very weak.
A cold is bad. A sour throat is very bad.

items: Mr. Casanova speaks clearly and Mr. Eugenio does, too.
Mr. Casanova speaks as clearly as Mr. Eugenio.

items.q: I can speak English well. I can speak Spanish well, too.
Mexico City has many skyscrapers. New York has many skyscrapers, too.
The Psychology book is interesting. The Astrology book is also interesting.
Dorothy is beautiful. Carla is beautiful, too.
John works slowly. Paul works slowly, too.
My mother is very careful. My father is also very careful.
